newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans investigated for Nazi salutes at match.
newsitem.headline: Germans investigated for Nazi salutes at match.

text.p: Justice authorities in Berlin are investigating two known soccer hooligans on suspicion of shouting racist abuse and giving Nazi salutes at a soccer friendly in Poland in September, a spokesman said on Thursday.

Police searched the men's homes and discovered documents which pointed to one of them having connections with right-wing extremist groups. He confessed to giving the straight-armed Nazi salute, made by Nazi soldiers in World War Two.

Around 500 German fans at the match shouted Nazi slogans, waved banners with Nazi slogans and burned a Polish flag. Polish and German fans traded obscenities and threw pieces of broken benches at each other before police in riot gear intervened.

Berlin Justice Ministry spokesman Ruediger Reiff said prosecutors argued that the Nazi salute, banned in Germany, was intended as a provocation to be seen on television at home and a crime had therefore been committed in Germany.
